verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Color-coded routing overlays (matching the Cable Routing Legend on page 4) appear to continue without a visible break: rooftop Cable Routing photos -> a wall-embedded DC conduit with a marked path down the wall -> orange/green LA and AC-earthing lines along the parapet and down a narrow gap between building sections -> the indoor Equipment Location diagram (Main meter/Solar meter/DCDB-ACDB/Battery) -> the Earth Pit Location photos showing DC/AC/LA pit markers together. However, since the building is still under construction, most of this 'routing' is a planned line overlay drawn on bare walls/roof rather than physically installed cable; only one photo shows an actual embedded conduit segment, and no cable-ties or clipping hardware are visible anywhere else in the run.
verdicts.rationale: The planned route is logically continuous with no orphan segments in the annotations, but because the cables are largely not yet physically installed (only design overlays on an under-construction building), true physical continuity and clipping/conduit compliance cannot be confirmed from these photos and should be re-verified after installation.
